sections.text: This Act may be called the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. It extends to the whole of India.
This Act applies to any person who is a Hindu by religion or is a Buddhist, Jain, or Sikh.

In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires: (a) 'custom' means any rule which has been continuously and uniformly observed; (b) 'degree of prohibited relationship' shall have the meaning assigned; (c) 'sapinda relationship' shall be construed accordingly.

A marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus if: (a) neither has a spouse living at the time; (b) both are capable of giving valid consent; (c) the bridegroom has completed 21 years and the bride 18 years; (d) the parties are not within prohibited degrees; (e) the parties are not sapindas of each other.
Where a minor bride is concerned, the consent of the guardian is required.
A Hindu marriage may be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party.
The State Government may make rules for the registration of Hindu marriages.
When either the husband or wife has withdrawn from the society of the other without reasonable excuse, the aggrieved party may apply to the court for restitution of conjugal rights.
Either party to a marriage may present a petition for judicial separation on any of the grounds specified in section 13.
Any marriage solemnized after the commencement of this Act shall be null and void if it contravenes conditions specified in section 5.
A marriage may be annulled on grounds including: (a) impotency; (b) unsoundness of mind; (c) consent obtained by force or fraud; (d) pregnancy by another person at the time of marriage.

A marriage may be dissolved by a decree of divorce on the following grounds: (a) adultery; (b) cruelty; (c) desertion for two years; (d) conversion to another religion; (e) unsoundness of mind; (f) leprosy; (g) venereal disease; (h) renunciation of the world; (i) not heard of as alive for seven years; (j) no resumption of cohabitation after one year of judicial separation; (k) no restitution of conjugal rights for one year after decree.
In any proceeding under section 13, the court may grant a decree of judicial separation instead of divorce.

Both parties to a marriage may present a petition for divorce by mutual consent. They must be living separately for one year and agree that the marriage has broken down. The court shall pass a decree after six months but before 18 months from the date of petition.

sections.section_title: No petition for divorce within one year of marriage
sections.text: No petition for divorce shall be presented within one year of marriage except in exceptional hardship cases.
Where a marriage has been dissolved, either party may remarry after the appeal period has expired.
Children born of void or voidable marriages shall be legitimate.
Any person who marries while a spouse is living shall be punished under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Whoever contravenes the conditions of marriage shall be punished.

sections.section_title: Court to which petition shall be presented
sections.text: Every petition under this Act shall be presented to the District Court within whose jurisdiction the marriage was solemnized or the parties reside.
Every petition shall contain facts and be verified by the petitioner.
The provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure apply to proceedings under this Act.
The court may order that proceedings be held in camera.
The court shall decree relief if satisfied that grounds exist and there is no legal bar.

sections.section_title: Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings
sections.text: Where either party has no independent income, the court may order the other party to pay maintenance during the proceedings and litigation expenses.
The court may grant permanent alimony and maintenance to either party at the time of passing any decree.
The court may make orders for the custody, maintenance, and education of minor children.
The court may make provisions for the disposal of joint property.
All decrees and orders are appealable as decrees under CPC.
This Act does not affect marriages solemnized under other personal laws or special marriage acts.
